content:
The image shows a severely desiccated, brown/tan leaf that appears completely dead and dried out. It is curled and shriveled with extensive necrosis across the entire leaf surface. There are no white powdery coatings (ruling out Powdery Mildew), no black sooty deposits (ruling out Sooty Mould), and no discrete dark lesions with concentric rings typical of Anthracnose.

The complete browning, drying, and death of the leaf tip/tissue is consistent with **Die Back** — a condition where tissue progressively dies from the tip or margins inward, resulting in complete necrosis and desiccation of affected parts.
